display.text: Does buying QQQ after a 25% drop from its all-time high, and selling when it gets back to that high, beat holding it?

display.message: The app holds QQQ from March 10, 1999 up to yesterday. It's all real data, nothing simulated, but it's split-adjusted only (dividends aren't counted), and its quality tier is "exercise only", so any result is a test of the method rather than a firm finding. Your rule is all set: buy after a 25% drop from the all-time high, sell when it gets back to that high, and repeat. Your cash earns no interest while it waits. Two choices left.

questions.question: What period should the test cover?

options.label: All the data, from March 1999
options.hint: Includes the dot-com crash, which took about 15 years to get back to its old high, so it's a long wait in cash or a long hold

options.label: The past 10 years (from Oct 2016)
options.hint: Short, and probably only one or two entries

options.label: Higher annual return
options.hint: Hardest test for a strategy that spends time in cash

options.label: Smaller worst loss
options.hint: Focuses on how deep it fell

options.label: Return relative to worst loss (Calmar)
options.hint: Balances growth against the deepest drop

form.prompt: Does buying QQQ after a 25% drop from its all-time high, and selling when it gets back to that high, beat holding it?

/universe/assets/0/security_id.note: QQQ resolves to the same security at both ends of the range. Data quality tier is exercise_only: results test the pipeline rather than make a finding.

/date_range/start.note: No range given. Data starts 1999-03-10; starting there includes the dot-com crash, which QQQ took about 15 years to recover from.

/strategy/exit/rules.quote: selling when it gets back to that high

/benchmarks.note: QQQ buy-and-hold is the comparison asked for; SPY added by default.

/robustness/oos_split.note: No parameter is swept, so there is nothing to optimize in-sample.

/cash/yield.note: No interest on cash while waiting; understates a strategy that sits in cash for long stretches.
